items.title: Expedia B2B Is Mostly Hotels, But It Wants a One-Stop Shop
items.summary: Expedia Group's B2B offering has been predominantly hotels. The online travel agency, which was founded more than 25 years ago, only recently began offering flights to B2B partners. Its strategy is to expand B2B into many more verticals.

items.title: Thank You, Google. Trivago Expects EU Tailwind
items.summary: A more even playing field for Trivago and Google's online competitors in Europe at long last? As the saying goes, the devil will be in the details.

items.title: Choice Hotels’ New Interim CEO’s First Task: Fix the Revenue Gap
items.summary: Dom Dragisich has had the top job for 11 weeks, having inherited a franchise machine that is adding rooms again but lagging rivals on revenue. He's making the pitch that he can close the gap.

items.title: Two Disneys: Booming U.S. Parks, Sluggish Asia
items.summary: While domestic park attendance remains strong, executives said Disney’s Asian parks aren’t immune to recent macroeconomic pressures.

items.title: Skift Capital Allocation Brief: A New Quarterly Read on Where Travel’s Money Goes
items.summary: M&A, venture money, buybacks, take-privates, a free quarterly read on all the capital moving through travel, what it means, and a first look at the decision intelligence Skift is building.

items.title: Delta Is Poaching Allegiant Pilots — and Now Allegiant Is Cutting Flights
items.summary: Allegiant pilots based in Minneapolis are leaving for Delta, causing Allegiant to further reduce flying out of the region.

items.title: Gatwick Is Set To Expand — And So Will Its Carbon Footprint
items.summary: The green-light could set precedent for other UK airports that have committed to curbing emissions but are also eyeing expansion — the question is whether growth and sustainability are compatible.

items.title: Air India Names New CEO: Former Ethiopian Airlines Boss to Lead Turnaround
items.summary: Tewolde Gebremariam coming in as Air India CEO was definitely not in our bingo card, but it may be exactly the kind of operator the airline needs for its next phase.
